title: Greenline — a SaaS landing page for test automation
description: A polished marketing page for Greenline, a fictional test-automation product, with a live animated test-run dashboard in the hero, a strip of made-up customer logos and ARIA feature tabs. It also has a monthly/annual pricing toggle with exact 20% discount math, a plan comparison table, a swipeable testimonial carousel, an FAQ accordion, and a cookie banner that remembers your choice.
prompt: Build me a polished SaaS marketing landing page for a fictional test-automation product called Greenline. I want a hero with an animated product mock (a test run dashboard), a logo strip of fictional customers, feature tabs, a monthly/annual pricing toggle with correct discount math, a comparison table, a testimonial carousel that works with the keyboard and swipe, an FAQ accordion with proper aria-expanded, and a dismissible cookie banner that remembers the choice. Make it clearly fictional, no real brands, and make it something I'd be happy to show a design team.

methodology: Pricing oracle computed in the spec: the annual price is the monthly price × 0.8, the yearly total is 12 × that, and the saving is 12 × monthly minus the yearly total. The rendered text is compared for each paid plan, and the toggle state survives a reload.

ARIA pattern conformance: the tabs use aria-selected, a roving tabindex, and arrow/Home/End keys with wrap-around; the accordion uses aria-expanded, aria-controls and labelled regions; the carousel uses aria-roledescription, aria-current dots and aria-hidden on inactive slides.
Input-modality coverage for the carousel: buttons, dots, arrow keys, and synthetic pointer swipes, including a mostly-vertical drag that must not change the slide.
Persistence: the cookie banner appears on first visit, remembers Accept and Decline separately in localStorage, and comes back when the key is removed.

Time-driven hero mock on page.clock: four workers busy after 2 s, the run finishes with 23 passed and 1 flaky within 15 s of fake time, then the next run number starts; reduced motion shows the finished run at once.
Screenshots at 1280px and 390px, the mobile menu, and the wide-font overflow check at 360–412px.
risks: Floating-point rounding in the discount math (for example 0.8 × 49 = 39.2 rendered as 39.199999); prices are rounded to cents and formatted with toLocaleString.
The sticky nav and the fixed back link overlapping on small screens; the logo is offset to leave room.
Carousel swipe misfiring during vertical page scrolls on phones; swipes need 40px of mostly horizontal movement.
The hero animation running forever in background tabs; it is a cheap 200 ms interval and stops completely under reduced motion.
qa.playwright: Most of this page follows standard ARIA patterns, so role-based locators (getByRole('tab'), getByRole('region', { name })) serve as the assertion and the accessibility check at once. The discount math is recomputed in the test rather than hard-coded, so a price change can't hide a formula bug. Swipes are sent with locator.dispatchEvent('pointerdown'/'pointerup') and clientX coordinates, which works the same on the desktop and Pixel 7 touch profiles without depending on the touchscreen API. The hero mock is the one timing-sensitive part: page.clock.install then pauseAt, then runFor in one-second steps until the run reports done, which is robust to small changes in spec durations. Reduced motion is checked with emulateMedia.
coverage: Monthly vs annual prices, yearly totals and savings; toggle persisted
Feature tabs by click, arrows, End, wrap-around and roving tabindex
Carousel buttons, wrap, dots, keyboard, swipe left/right and ignoring vertical drags
FAQ aria-expanded, labelled regions, independent panels
Hero test-run mock on a fake clock and under reduced motion

a11y: Tabs, accordion, switch and carousel follow the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices patterns with full keyboard support. The billing toggle is a role=switch with a label, the comparison table uses row and column headers and scrolls inside a focusable region, and the animated mock is a labelled image that becomes static under reduced motion.
